If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to capture bullish momentum.

If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid overestimating downside risk.

If sentiment shifts from negative to positive over 3–5 days, accelerate upward slope in mid-horizon (8–15 days) by 0.3–0.8% per day to reflect sentiment reversal.

If sentiment remains flat (0.33–0.67) across 5+ days, apply linear smoothing to forecast path in late horizon (16–30 days) to avoid overreacting to noise.

If sentiment spikes to 1.00 in last 2 days, add 0.2–0.5% upward bias to late horizon (20–30 days) to reflect strong conviction.

If sentiment drops to 0.00 in last 2 days, apply 0.2–0.5% downward bias to late horizon (20–30 days) to reflect bearish sentiment override.
